definitions.explanation: A structure built along a waterfront where ships can load and unload cargo or passengers. Often evokes an atmospheric, slightly nostalgic image of port towns.

examples.japanese: {波止場|はとば}に{船|ふね}が{停|と}まっている。
examples.english: A ship is moored at the wharf.

examples.japanese: {波止場|はとば}で{魚釣|さかなつ}りをしている{人|ひと}がいた。
examples.english: There were people fishing at the pier.

examples.japanese: {夕暮|ゆうぐ}れの{波止場|はとば}を{散歩|さんぽ}するのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like strolling along the wharf at dusk.

notes:
USAGE:
A somewhat literary or evocative word. In everyday speech, {港|みなと} (port, harbor) is more common. {波止場|はとば} often appears in literature, songs, and nostalgic descriptions of port towns.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {波止場|はとば}で{待|ま}つ (to wait at the wharf)
- {波止場|はとば}の{風景|ふうけい} (wharf scenery)
- {波止場|はとば}で{働|はたら}く (to work at the docks)

FORMS:
{波止|はと} (breakwater) + {場|ば} (place). {波止|はと} comes from {波|なみ} (wave) + {止|と}める (to stop).
